# About Suneung Chegam Research Lab

## Company Overview

| Core product | Notebooks designed in the same format as Korean CSAT exam papers |

| Sales channel | Naver Smart Store (no standalone online store) |

```
Instagram content exposure
       ↓
Brand/product search
       ↓
```

## Business Pain Points & Project Overview

| Pain Point 1 | Pain Point 2 | Pain Point 3 |
|--------|--------|--------|
| **Unclear branding direction** | **Low repeat-purchase rate** | **Unclear profitability structure** |
| "How should the brand grow?" | "Customers buy once and do not return." | "Should shipping fees be raised? Are margins sufficient?" |

**Project scope:**

- Analysis period: 2026.02.01 ~ 2026.04.30 (three months)

# Core KPI Framework

## Rationale for KPI Selection

Pain Point → KPI mapping:

| Business issue | Selected KPI | Rationale |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Profitability stability | Net profit margin, contribution profit by product | Focus on actual profit rather than revenue alone |
| Shipping-cost efficiency | Shipping-cost share, AOV | Shipping cost relative to AOV matters more than the absolute amount |
| Repeat-purchase improvement | Repeat-purchase rate, funnel conversion rate | Retention is critical to profitability |
| Marketing direction | CVR by channel, RPV | Evidence is needed to prioritize high-ROI channels |
| Branding | Branded-keyword CVR, interested-customer growth | Assess whether branding translates into sales |

---

## AS-IS / TO-BE

| Category | AS-IS (Current) | TO-BE (Target) |
|------|------------|------------|
| Marketing | Reliance on Instagram viral traffic as a single channel | Combine Naver Search ads, Instagram, and Shopping optimization |
| Coupon strategy | Coupons issued without product-level targeting | Issue coupons on the 18th–20th of each month, targeting higher-margin options such as Lavender and Science |
| Repeat purchase | Customer drop-off after the first purchase (repeat-purchase rate 9.6–11.1%) | Build a repeat-purchase cycle with automated follow-up coupons |
| new product | Unsystematic launch timing and process | Saturday launch → Sunday coupon → D+4 reminder |
| Core products | White and Gray lead revenue but have the lowest margins due to residual packaging capacity | Use 10-unit bundles to improve box utilization and narrow margin differences across options |
| Profit structure | Many single-item orders create unused box capacity and shipping-cost inefficiency | Raise AOV above ₩20,000 and encourage 10-unit purchases to reduce shipping-cost share |

---

## Overview of Three Dashboards

| Category | Dashboard 1 | Dashboard 2 | Dashboard 3 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| Name | Profit Margin Analysis | Sales Operations Analysis | Product/Channel Strategy |

# Data Sources & ERD

## Data Sources

**Smart Store exported data**

```
├── Sales performance          (purchasers, payment amount, coupons, and refunds by date, weekday, and time)
├── Customer status          (total, new, and returning customers; cumulative interested customers)
├── Product performance          (purchases, payment amount, and refunds by product name and product ID)
├── product_shopping_behavior (product detail views and view-to-purchase conversion)
├── product_marketing_channel    (channel group/name and purchase contribution by product)
├── product_search_channel      (keywords, channels, and purchase contribution by product)
├── product_demographics      (purchase distribution by gender and age for each product)
├── product_customer_profile_occupation (buyer occupation distribution by product)
├── product_region          (regional purchase distribution by product)
├── all_channels           (visits, purchases, and revenue by channel group/name)
├── search_channels           (visits, CVR, and RPV by keyword)
├── demographics           (purchase distribution by gender, age, and channel)
├── shipping_statistics           (dispatch compliance and average delivery time by shipping type)
├── smartstore_purchase_confirmations (order ID, product ID, quantity, fees, and settlement amount)
├── smartstore_orders    (order status, product name, option, and buyer information)
├── smartstore_cancellations    (cancellation and refund details)
├── settlement_by_order      (fee breakdown and settlement status by order)
├── settlement_by_item    (fee details by item)
└── daily_settlement      (daily settlement amount and total fees)
```

**Company-provided cost data**

```
├── Purchase cost by product  (Math/other subjects ₩2,000; Chegam Pad ₩4,000 — based on product ID)
├── Packaging cost (A4: ₩250 per box, up to 10 units combined · Pad: ₩500 per unit)
└── Shipping cost (fixed at ₩2,500 per order)
```

## Tableau Calculated Fields (Margin Calculation)

### Cost Structure 

| Item | Product ID | Details |
|------|---------|------|
| Math notebook purchase cost | 11868416127 | ₩2,000 per unit |
| Other-subject notebook purchase cost | 13031541573 | ₩2,000 per unit |
| Chegam Pad purchase cost | 13318342227 | ₩4,000 per unit |
| A4 Packaging cost | — | Up to 10 units per box; ₩250 per box |
| Pad packaging cost | — | ₩500 per unit (packed separately from A4 products) |
| Shipping cost | — | Fixed at ₩2,500 per order |

::: {.neutral-callout}
**Combined-packaging policy:** A4 notebooks are combined in one box for every 10 units, while pads are packaged separately. Packaging cost is therefore calculated by product type.
:::

---

### Tableau Calculated Fields

The dashboard uses a five-layer calculation structure covering product classification, packaging cost, revenue and fees, margin calculation, and KPI aggregation.

<details class="formula-details">
<summary>View Tableau Calculated Fields</summary>

<div class="formula-body" markdown="1">

```sql
// ════════════════════════════════════════
// LAYER 1. Product classification and cost
// ════════════════════════════════════════

// 1. Product type
// Classify Pad vs. A4 by product ID
IF STR([Product ID]) = "13318342227"
THEN "Pad"
ELSE "A4"
END

// 2. Purchase cost
// Pad ₩4,000 / A4 (Math and other subjects) ₩2,000
IF STR([Product ID]) = "13318342227"
THEN 4000
ELSE 2000
END

// 3. Product cost  [row level]
[Purchase cost] * [Quantity]

// 4. Product cost by order  [FIXED]
// Aggregate by order ID to prevent duplication
{ FIXED [Order ID] : SUM([Product cost]) }


// ════════════════════════════════════════
// LAYER 2. Packaging cost
// A4: one box per 10 units; Pad: packaged separately
// ════════════════════════════════════════

// 5. A4 order quantity  [FIXED]
{ FIXED [Order ID] :
  SUM(IF [Product type] = "A4" THEN [Quantity] ELSE 0 END) }

// 6. Pad order quantity  [FIXED]
{ FIXED [Order ID] :
  SUM(IF [Product type] = "Pad" THEN [Quantity] ELSE 0 END) }

// 7. A4 Packaging cost
// One box per 10 units (₩250), rounded up using CEILING
IF [A4 order quantity] > 0
THEN CEILING([A4 order quantity] / 10) * 250
ELSE 0
END

// 8. Pad packaging cost
// ₩500 per Pad
[Pad order quantity] * 500

// 9. Total cost
[Product cost by order] + [A4 Packaging cost] + [Pad packaging cost]


// ════════════════════════════════════════
// LAYER 3. Revenue and costs (Naver Smart Store)
// ════════════════════════════════════════

// 10. Revenue by order  [FIXED]
{ FIXED [Order ID] : SUM([Final total order amount by product]) }

// 11. Shipping cost by order  [FIXED]
// Fixed at ₩2,500 per order
{ FIXED [Order ID] : MIN(2500) }

// 12. Revenue-linked fees by order  [FIXED]
{ FIXED [Order ID] : SUM([Revenue-linked fees]) }

// 13. Naver Pay order-management fees by order  [FIXED]
{ FIXED [Order ID] : SUM([Naver Pay order-management fees]) }


// ════════════════════════════════════════
// LAYER 4. Margin calculation
// ════════════════════════════════════════

// 14. Margin by order
[Revenue by order]
- [Total cost]
- [Shipping cost by order]
- [Revenue-linked fees by order]
- [Naver Pay order-management fees by order]

// 15. Margin  [row level / format: percentage]
[Margin by order] / [Revenue by order]

// 16. Margin by product  [weighted average reflecting sales volume]
SUM([Margin by order]) / SUM([Revenue by order])

// 17. Margin by option  [LOD — Smart Store product name + option level]
{ FIXED [Smart Store product name], [Option name] :
  SUM([Margin by order]) / SUM([Revenue by order]) }


// ════════════════════════════════════════
// LAYER 5. KPI cards
// Use FIXED by order ID + MIN to prevent duplicate aggregation
// ════════════════════════════════════════

// 18. Net profit card
SUM({ FIXED [Order ID] : MIN([Margin by order]) })

// 19. Average margin card  [format: percentage]
SUM({ FIXED [Order ID] : MIN([Margin by order]) })
/
SUM({ FIXED [Order ID] : MIN([Revenue by order]) })

```

</div>
</details>

## Three-month Profit Structure Comparison

| Metric | February | March | April | Trend |
|------|-----|-----|-----|------|
| Total revenue | ₩7,760,500 | ₩12,948,610 | ₩9,436,000 | March peak |
| Net profit | ₩3,307,951 | ₩5,184,863 | ₩3,055,347 | Same pattern |
| Margin | 43.90% | 41.89% | 42.33% | **Stable** |
| AOV | ₩12,891 | ₩12,356 | ₩14,126 | April high |
| Purchasers | 535 customers | 832 customers | 539 customers | March peak |
| Shipping-cost share | 17.4% | 16.6% | 15.6% | Improving |

**Profit-structure waterfall (March):**

```
Total revenue  ₩12,375,900  (100%)
  - Product cost  ₩5,378,000  (43.5%)
  - Shipping cost    ₩2,052,500  (16.6%)
  - fees      ₩543,213  ( 4.4%)
  - Packaging cost   ₩303,750  ( 2.5%)
  = Net profit    ₩4,098,437  (33.1%)
```

::: {.insight-box}
**Key diagnosis:** Margins remained stable at 40–44% over three months, indicating a fundamentally healthy profit structure.
The relatively high shipping-cost share is driven by low AOV; raising AOV above ₩20,000 should take priority over increasing shipping fees.
:::

---

## Key Anomaly — "Record-High AOV, but Revenue and Net Profit Fell Sharply"

| | March | April | Interpretation |
|--|-----|-----|------|
| Purchasers | 832 customers | 539 customers | **-35.2% Sharp decline** |
| AOV | ₩12,356 | ₩14,126 | **+14.3% Increase** |
| Total revenue | ₩12,948,610 | ₩9,436,000 | -27.1% Decline |

> **In April, fewer customers purchased, but those who did spent more.**  
> This suggests stronger high-intent purchasing (repeat or bundle purchases) but weaker new-customer conversion.

---

## Product Margin Matrix — "High Sales ≠ High Profit"

```
              High margin (50%+)
                    ↑
  Lavender(April 51.8%) │  Social Studies(March 56.99%) ★Coupon priority
  Baby Pink        │  new Science(52.16%)  ★Coupon priority
──────────────────────────────────→ High revenue
  Chalkboard Green          │  White ← revenue #1, combined packaging lower packaging efficiency
  Baby Pink        │  Gray ← High revenue, combined packaging lower packaging efficiency
              Low margin (40% range)
```

**Three-month margin summary by option:**


| Option | Peak Margin | Average Revenue Share | Strategy |
|------|-----------|------------|------|
| Social Studies | 56.99% (March) | Low | Coupon priority |
| New Science | 52.16% (Mar 29) | Medium | Coupon priority |
| Lavender | 51.80% (April) | Medium | Coupon priority |
| White | 44.26% (April) | Highest | Exclude from coupon priority |
| Gray | 45.68% (3/29) | High | Exclude from coupon priority |
| Exam-Paper Size | 42.08% (Apr 1) | Rapid growth | Monitor for 1–2 additional months before designating it as a core option |

::: {.strategy-box}
**Strategic recommendation:** White and Gray were already high-volume core options before coupons were issued. Additional coupons may therefore discount purchases that would have occurred anyway, reducing margins. Prioritize coupons for lower-volume options with greater margin headroom to stimulate incremental purchases and balance sales across options.
:::

---

## 4.5 Shipping-Cost Structure & AOV Strategy

::: {.neutral-callout}
Shipping cost ₩2,500 → ₩3,200 under consideration for increase
:::

**Shipping-cost share vs. industry benchmarks:**

| Category | Shipping-cost share | Description |
|------|-----------|------|
| General e-commerce average | 3~8% | Large platforms / in-house logistics |
| Small Smart Store sellers | 8~15% | Individual/small-business sellers |
| **Suneung Chegam Research Lab** | **15.6~17.4%** | Current level |

::: {.neutral-callout}
The product is low-priced and relatively bulky, which structurally increases shipping-cost share.

For products with an AOV of ₩12,000–14,000, a shipping fee of ₩3,000–3,500 can account for roughly one quarter of the selling price.
This makes the shipping-cost share appear structurally high even when the absolute shipping fee is not unusual.

→ Shipping cost is not inherently expensive; rather, **the low unit price makes shipping appear disproportionately large**
:::

::: {.strategy-box}
**Recommended direction:** Rather than increasing shipping fees, introduce a **free-shipping threshold around ₩20,000** and encourage bundled purchases to raise AOV.

:::

## Repeat-Purchase Structure — Three-month Trend

**Joint analysis of repeat-purchase and funnel conversion rates:**

```
         Interested customers    →   Total orders   →   Returning Customers   Repeat-purchase rate
February:     5,772 customers        535 customers          50 customers       9.6%
March:     7,830 customers        832 customers          65 customers      11.1%  ← peak
April:    11,037 customers        539 customers          59 customers      11.0%  ← risk signal
```

**Funnel conversion rate:**

```
February: 5,772 → 535 =  9.3%
March: 7,830 → 832 = 10.6%
April: 11,037 → 539 =  4.9% ← lowest observed
```

::: {.neutral-callout}
**Key issue:** April recorded the highest number of interested customers (11,037), yet the purchase conversion rate fell to **4.9%, the lowest of the three months**.
→ Awareness is increasing, but a **first-purchase barrier** remains
:::

---

## Customer Conversion Funnel Analysis

Three-month trend in interested customers: **5,772 → 7,830 → 11,037** (steady increase)  
However, purchasers changed from **535 → 832 → 539**, showing a sharp decline after March.

> **"Traffic is growing, but conversion is not"**  
> Brand awareness is building, but conversion friction remains  
> → First-purchase incentives (discount coupons or trial bundles) are needed

---

## Identifying High-Conversion Purchase Windows

| Day | Peak Purchase Window | Representative Orders | Purchase Pattern |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **Sunday** | **18–21h** | 56 orders (Mar 29) | Weekend evening planned purchases |
| **Thursday** | **0–6h** | 47 orders (March) | Late-night impulse purchases |
| **Wednesday** | **21–24h** | 59 orders (Mar 25–31) | Weekday late-night purchases |
| Saturday | 9~12h + 21~24h | Bimodal pattern | Morning and late-night split |

**Optimal content publishing schedule:**

```
Monday: no scheduled content
Tuesday: —
Wednesday 9 PM: publish a post → drive purchases before midnight
Thursday 11 PM: publish a Story → drive late-night purchases
Friday: —
Saturday 9 AM: announce new product/event
Sunday 5 PM: coupon-expiry reminder → target the 6–9 PM purchase peak
```

# Business Insights — Deep Dives into Key Dates

## Insight 1 | Feb 11 (Wed) — Seasonality Effect

**₩1,226,700 (highest single-day revenue in February)**

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![ ](data:image/png;base64,){.dashboard-img}

![ ](data:image/png;base64,){.dashboard-img}
:::

| Metric | Feb 11 | February daily average | Comparison |
|------|---------|------------|------|
| Total revenue | ₩1,226,700 | ₩277,160 | **+343%** |
| Net profit | ₩595,327 | ₩118,141 | **+404%** |
| Average margin | **50.76%** | 43.90% | **+6.86%p** |
| AOV | **₩16,804** | ₩12,891 | **+30.4%** |
| Purchasers | 66 | 19.1/day | **+245%** |
| Coupon usage rate | **0.0%** | 0.0% | Same |
| Mobile payments | **99.4%** | 95.5% | +3.9%p |
| Repeat-purchase rate | **12.3%** | 9.6% | +2.7%p |

**Results of initial hypothesis tests:**

| Hypothesis | Result | Assessment |
|------|------|------|
| Seasonal demand surge immediately after the Lunar New Year holiday | Purchasers 3.5×, conversion rate 3.4× | Supported |
| A demand spike can occur without coupons | 0% coupon usage with an even higher margin | Supported |
| Increase in bundle purchases | Average units per purchase unchanged (2.7) | Rejected |
| Higher share of repeat customers | 12.3% (slightly above the typical 9.6%) | Partially supported |

::: {.neutral-callout}
**New key finding:**
"AOV (+30%), margin (+6.86 pp), and purchasers (+245%) all increased simultaneously."
Identifying how often such dates occur during the year should be the starting point for the marketing calendar.
:::

> **One-line takeaway:**  
> "Feb 11 delivered the highest margin without coupons; timing campaigns around the resumption of exam preparation may be more powerful than discounting."

→ A **14-day coupon validity window** would comfortably cover the observed 11-day cycle.
:::

**Coupon Cycle × Content Calendar:**

```
D-11 (coupon issuance): Instagram post announcing the coupon
D-8  (Wednesday night): Instagram Story reminder (leveraging the Wed 21–24h pattern: 59 orders)
D-4  (Thursday early morning): pre-midnight post (leveraging the Thu 0–6h pattern: 39 orders)
D-0  (Sunday evening): "Ends today" urgency Story (leveraging the Sun 18–21h pattern: 56 orders)
```

**Coupon Operations Playbook:**

| Scenario | Recommended Issue Date | Rationale |
|------|-----------|------|
| Regular monthly cycle | **18th–20th of each month** | Position peak usage near month-end, ~11 days later |
| Seasonal campaign | ~10 days before the seasonal event | Align peak coupon use with the seasonal demand peak |
| 100 days before the CSAT | D-110 | Target peak coupon usage around D-100 |

**Redesign coupon targeting:**

::: {.neutral-callout}
**Current issue:** Coupons were concentrated on White, Gray, and Exam-Paper Size, all relatively low-margin options (roughly 38–45%).

**Recommended redesign:** Issue dedicated coupons for Lavender, New Science, and Baby Pink, where margins are roughly 49–52%.  
Exclude White and Gray from priority couponing or apply a lower discount rate.
:::

**Link to the Repeat-Purchase Problem:**

- Final-week repeat-purchase rate was only 4.6%, suggesting that many new customers purchased once and did not return.
- Design an automated **second-purchase coupon three weeks after the first purchase**.
- If some of the 146 purchasers from Mar 29 can be retained, the April repeat-purchase rate could improve.

> **One-line takeaway:**  
> "Coupon usage peaked 11 days after issuance (Mar 18 → Mar 29), and 67% of March revenue was concentrated in the final seven days. Fixing coupon issuance around the 18th–20th of each month may reproduce a similar pattern, but the timing effect should be validated over an additional 2–3 months."

## Supporting Insight | Three-month Cumulative Product Performance (Dashboard 3)

**Three-Month Cumulative Product Performance:**

| Product | Three-Month Revenue | Units Sold | Coupon Spend | Refund Amount | Refund Rate |
|--------|--------------|---------|-----------|--------|---------|
| [Math] Suneung Chegam A4 Mock-Exam Notebook | **₩20,411,300** | 4,345 | ₩530,200 | ₩690,330 | 3.38% |
| [Korean/English/Social Studies] Suneung Chegam A4 Mock-Exam Notebook | ₩5,227,760 | 1,072 | ₩80,640 | ₩254,820 | **4.87%** |
| [Math] Suneung Chegam Exam-Paper Size Notebook | ₩3,405,350 | 418 | **₩395,630** | ₩95,630 | **2.81%** |
| [Legal Pad] Suneung Chegam Exam-Paper Size Notebook | ₩498,700 | 63 | ₩70,110 | ₩18,260 | 3.66% |

**Interpretation by Product:**

::: {.insight-box}
**① Coupon Concentration on Exam-Paper Size**  
Coupon spend as a share of Exam-Paper Size revenue: ₩395,630 / ₩3,405,350 = **11.6%**, about 4.5× the Math A4 ratio (2.6%).  
→ This suggests coupons were more effective at **lowering the first-purchase barrier for a new product** than at driving repeat purchases of established products.

**② Refund Rate as a Quality Signal**  
- Korean/English/Social Studies A4: refund rate **4.87%**, the only product group above 4% → monitor for possible expectation mismatch.
- Exam-Paper Size: **2.81%**, the lowest refund rate → encouraging satisfaction despite being a new product.

**③ Lowest Coupon Efficiency: Legal Pad**  
Legal Pad coupon spend (₩70,110) was high relative to its revenue (₩498,700).  
→ **Exclude it from coupon priority or reposition it within bundles.**
:::

::: {.strategy-box}
**Coupons should not simply be allocated to products that already sell well; they should be used to reduce the first-purchase barrier for products the business wants to grow.**

**Replication Formula:**

| Item | Details |
|------|------|
| Timing | 2–3 weeks after a new-product launch, once awareness has formed |
| Target | Higher-priced products with low refund rates |
| Method | Send Exam-Paper Size coupons to Math A4 purchasers (cross-selling) |
| Expected Impact | Reproduce a high-revenue day similar to Mar 26 while accelerating early sales of the new product |

:::

## Replicability of the March Peak

**Why March Was the Strongest Month — Replicable Conditions:**

Several factors occurred simultaneously in March:

1. First introduction of coupons (0% → 4.9%)
2. Launch of the Exam-Paper Size product and new options (New Science, New Social Studies, Chalkboard Green)
3. Highest purchaser count (832)
4. Highest repeat-purchase rate (11.1%)

::: {.insight-box}
**The combination of a new-product launch and coupon introduction appears to have been central to March performance.**

Coupons remained active in April, but no comparable new-product stimulus occurred, and performance declined.  
→ **Strategy: test a new option or limited edition each month to evaluate whether the March effect can be replicated.**

Examples:

- May → new color option + coupon
- June → CSAT D-100 edition + coupon
- August → special edition before Chuseok + coupon
:::

| March | 7,830 | 832 | 10.6% | 65 | **11.1%** ← Peak |
| April | **11,037** | 539 | **4.9%** ← Lowest | 59 | 11.0% |

::: {.neutral-callout}
**Key April anomaly:** April had the highest number of interested customers (11,037) but the lowest purchase conversion rate (4.9%).

Awareness is building steadily, but a barrier is discouraging first purchases. First-purchase incentives such as discount coupons or trial bundles are warranted.
:::

The pattern can be verified directly by filtering the following periods in Dashboard 2.

| Check | Filter (start–end date) | What to examine |
|------------|------------------------|------------|
| March vs. April repeat-purchase rate | Apply 3/1–3/31 and 4/1–4/30 separately | Coupons remained active (~4.7%), but repeat-purchase rate stayed flat → retention tactics beyond coupons are needed |
| Wednesday-night purchase surge | Filter 3/1–3/31 | Wednesday 21–24h orders were 2.8× February levels → recurring late-night purchase pattern |
| Apr 28 purchaser rebound | Filter 4/1–4/30 | Verify the Apr 28 rebound within the broader downward trend and trace its trigger |



#### Optimal Purchase Timing — Three-Month Heatmap Summary

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![February Purchase Heatmap](data:image/png;base64,)

![March Purchase Heatmap](data:image/png;base64,)

![April Purchase Heatmap](data:image/png;base64,)
:::

| Month | Peak Purchase Window | Orders | Pattern |
|----|--------------|------|------|
| February | Sunday 21–24h | 32 | Weekend late night |
| March | Wednesday 21–24h | 76 | Weekday late night |
| April | Wednesday 21–24h | 31 | Weekday late night |

Common three-month pattern: **Purchases concentrate after 9 PM, with recurring Wednesday late-night peaks.**

::: {.insight-box}
**21–24h Purchase Pattern:** Purchases were consistently strongest in the 21–24h window. March Wednesday 21–24h reached 76 orders, 2.8× the previous month. Given the repeated Wednesday/Thursday late-night pattern, **publishing Instagram content around 9 PM on Wednesday** appears to be the most promising timing for conversion.
:::

### Dashboard 3 | Product/Channel Strategy Analysis Results

#### Channel Investment Priority — RPV × CVR

| Channel | CVR | RPV | Investment Priority |
|------|-----|-----|-------------|
| Naver Search | **39%** (6.5× median) | **₩4,592** (6× median) | ★ 1st |
| Shopping (price comparison) | High | High | Optimize thumbnails and reviews |
| Google Search | Low | ₩735 | Reallocate budget to Naver |

::: {.strategy-box}
**Channel strategy conclusion:** Naver Search is the clear top-priority channel, with both CVR and RPV roughly six times the median. Reallocating part of the Google Ads budget toward Naver Search is therefore more attractive from an ROI perspective.
:::

---

#### Data Evidence Linking Branding to Sales

| Search Keyword | CVR |
|-----------|-----|
| Suneung Chegam Notebook (Korean branded query) | 21.4% |
| **Suneung Chegam Research Lab Notebook (Korean branded query)** | **23.9%** |

Customers searching with the brand name show a higher conversion rate. Interested customers also increased for three consecutive months (5,772 → 7,830 → 11,037), suggesting that brand awareness is increasingly translating into sales.

---

#### Dual-Target Content Strategy

| Target | Primary Channel | Revenue | Content Direction |
|------|---------|------|------------|
| Exam-takers (17–19) | Shopping | ₩3,455,490 | Exam-taker empathy-focused content |
| Parents (46–50) | Shopping | ₩3,301,460 | "Gift for a child" messaging |

Shopping revenue from parents aged 46–50 is comparable to that of exam-takers, suggesting meaningful parent-led purchasing. A dual-target strategy should therefore combine exam-taker-focused content with messaging positioned as a gift for one's child.

---

## Integrated Action Plan

| Strategy | Current State | Target State | Expected Impact |
|------|------|------|---------|
| Optimize coupon timing | Irregular issuance | Fixed issuance on the 18th–20th each month | Sustain late-month revenue concentration |
| Redesign coupon targeting | Coupons concentrated on low-margin products | Prioritize Social Studies, Lavender, and Science | Improve net profit with the same coupon spend |
| Shift White/Gray strategy | Primarily single-item sales | 10-unit bundle promotion | Improve box utilization and narrow margin gaps |
| Build repeat-purchase cycle | Customer drop-off after the first purchase | Automated follow-up coupon | Target repeat-purchase rate of 15%+ |
| Reallocate channel investment | Instagram-only dependence | Add Naver Search advertising | Scale a channel with 39% CVR |
| Standardize new-product launch process | Unstructured launches | Two-stage Sat→Sun launch | Replicate the D+1 launch surge |
| Increase AOV | ₩12,000–14,000 | ₩20,000+ bundle design | Reduce shipping cost as a share of order value |
| Protect revenue troughs | Irregular content | Scheduled content on the final Tuesday of each month | Test whether the Apr 28 rebound can be reproduced |
